Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip: Lie on the bench with your eyes just under the bar and your feet firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack the bar with straight arms.
Lower it with control until it brushes your lower chest, with your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
Press until your arms are straight without lifting your glutes off the bench.
Tip: with heavy weights, train with a spotter or use the safety bars.
Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Sit on the bench with the dumbbells on your thighs and lie back, bringing them to chest height.
With your palms facing your feet, press until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower with control until the dumbbells are beside your chest, elbows slightly below the bench.
Press back up. When you finish, bring the dumbbells to your thighs before sitting up.
Alternating_Floor_Press: Lie on your back on the floor with a kettlebell in each hand, elbows on the floor and knees bent.
Press one kettlebell until your arm is straight and lower it until your elbow touches the floor.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating. The floor limits the range and protects the shoulder.
Bench_Press_-_With_Bands: Pass the band behind your back at armpit height and hold one end in each hand.
Lie on a bench or on the floor with your hands beside your chest.
Press until your arms are straight and return with control, without letting the band snap you back.
Pushups: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders and straighten your legs, with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower by bending your elbows until your chest is close to the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your abs and glutes so your hips do not sag. If it is hard, rest on your knees.
Barbell_Incline_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Gri: Set the bench to about 30 degrees and lie down with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack it.
Lower it with control to your upper chest and press until your arms are straight.
Keep your glutes on the bench.
Incline_Dumbbell_Press: Set the bench to about 30 degrees and sit with the dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back, bringing them to shoulder height, and press until your arms are straight over your upper chest.
Lower with control until the dumbbells are beside your chest and press back up.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Floor_Press: Lie on your back on the floor with a kettlebell in one hand, elbow on the floor and knees bent.
Press until your arm is straight, keeping your wrist straight.
Lower until your elbow touches the floor. Do all the reps and switch arms.
Dips_-_Chest_Version: Support yourself on the parallel bars with your arms straight.
Lean your torso forward and lower by bending your elbows, which flare out slightly.
Go down until you feel a stretch in your chest (shoulders roughly level with your elbows) and push back up.
If your shoulders bother you, shorten the range.
Decline_Push-Up: Put your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor, slightly wider than your shoulders.
With your body in a straight line, lower until your face is close to the floor.
Push until your arms are straight. It works the upper chest and shoulders more.
Cable_Crossover: Set the pulleys high and grab a handle in each hand. Step forward with one foot in front.
With your elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring your hands together in front of your hips in an arc.
Squeeze your chest for a second and return with control until you feel the stretch.
Butterfly: Sit in the machine with your back supported and adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
With your elbows slightly bent, bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Squeeze for a second and return with control until you feel the stretch, without letting the weight pull on your shoulders.
Dumbbell_Flyes: Lie on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight over your chest and palms facing each other.
With your elbows slightly bent and fixed, open your arms out to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Close them again in an arc, as if hugging a tree.
Use a moderate weight: the shoulder is in a demanding position.
Cross_Over_-_With_Bands: Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Step forward and, with your elbows slightly bent, bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Return with control until your arms are out to the sides.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes: Set the bench to about 30 degrees and lie down with the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
With your elbows slightly bent, open your arms out to the sides until you feel the stretch.
Close them again in an arc.
Push-Up_Wide: Set up as for a push-up, but with your hands much wider than your shoulders.
Lower with your body in a straight line until your chest is close to the floor.
Push until your arms are straight. If your shoulders bother you, bring your hands in a little.
Barbell_Shoulder_Press: Standing or seated, with the bar resting in front of your shoulders and your hands slightly wider than them.
Squeeze your abs and glutes and press the bar straight up, moving your face back as it passes.
Finish with your arms straight and the bar overhead, then lower with control.
Do not arch your lower back to lift more weight.
Dumbbell_Shoulder_Press: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press until your arms are straight overhead without arching your back.
Lower with control to shoulder height.
Seated_Dumbbell_Press: Sit on a bench with an upright backrest and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower with control until the dumbbells are at ear height.
Kettlebell_Seated_Press: Sit on the floor with your legs straight or crossed and a kettlebell resting on your shoulder.
With your torso upright and your abs braced, press it until your arm is straight.
Lower with control. Since your legs cannot help, it demands core stability.
Shoulder_Press_-_With_Bands: Stand on the band with both feet and hold the ends at shoulder height.
Press until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower with control to shoulder height.
Handstand_Push-Ups: Kick up into a handstand against a wall, hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lower with control by bending your elbows until your head almost touches the floor.
Push until your arms are straight.
This is an advanced exercise: learn to hold a handstand first and put something soft under your head.
Side_Lateral_Raise: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your elbows slightly bent.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Lower with control. Do not swing your body: better a light weight and good technique.
Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise: Sit side-on next to a low pulley and grab the handle with the far hand.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, elbow slightly bent.
Lower with control. Do all the reps and switch sides.
Seated_Side_Lateral_Raise: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows slightly bent.
Lower with control. Sitting makes it harder to cheat with your body.
Lateral_Raise_-_With_Bands: Stand on the middle of the band and hold one end in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Kettlebell_Arnold_Press: Hold the kettlebell at shoulder height with your palm facing you.
Press upwards while rotating your wrist, so you finish with your palm facing forward and your arm straight.
Lower, undoing the rotation. Do all the reps and switch arms.
Face_Pull: Attach a rope to the pulley at face height and grab it with both hands.
Step back and pull the rope towards your face, separating your hands and taking your elbows high and back.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders for a second and return with control.
A good exercise for shoulder health; use a moderate weight.
Reverse_Flyes: Standing or seated, lean your torso forward with a straight back and a dumbbell in each hand under your chest.
With your elbows slightly bent, open your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second at the top and lower with control.
Seated_Bent-Over_Rear_Delt_Raise: Sit on the edge of a bench, lean your torso over your thighs and let a dumbbell hang in each hand.
Open your arms out to the sides with your elbows slightly bent, up to shoulder height.
Lower with control without straightening your torso.
Back_Flyes_-_With_Bands: Hold the band with both hands in front of your chest, arms straight.
Open your arms out to the sides until the band touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Band_Pull_Apart: Stand holding the band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight and hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull your hands apart, stretching the band until it touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return with control. It works well as a shoulder warm-up.
Triceps_Pushdown: Attach a bar or rope to the high pulley and grab it with your elbows at your sides.
Straighten your arms downwards without moving your elbows.
Squeeze for a second at the bottom and come up with control until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
Lying_Triceps_Press: Lie on the bench holding an EZ bar over your chest with your arms straight.
Without moving your elbows, bend them to lower the bar towards your forehead.
Straighten your arms to return to the top. Use a weight you can lower with full control.
Standing_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension: Stand holding a dumbbell with both hands overhead, arms straight.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head, elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Straighten your arms to return to the top without arching your back.
Band_Skull_Crusher: Lie down with the band anchored behind your head and hold the ends with your arms straight over your chest.
Without moving your elbows, bend them, bringing your hands towards your forehead.
Dips_-_Triceps_Version: Support yourself on the parallel bars with your arms straight and your body vertical.
Lower by bending your elbows, kept close to your body and pointing back.
Go down until your elbows are at about 90 degrees and push until your arms are straight.
Keep your torso upright so the triceps work more than the chest.
Push-Ups_-_Close_Triceps_Position: Set up as for a push-up, but with your hands under your chest, almost touching.
Lower with your elbows close to your body until your chest is near your hands.
Push until your arms are straight, keeping your body straight.
Bench_Dips: Place your hands on the edge of a bench behind you and stretch your legs out in front (or bend them to make it easier).
Lower by bending your elbows, which point back, until they are at about 90 degrees.
Push until your arms are straight. Do not go lower if your shoulders feel uncomfortable.
Isometric_Chest_Squeezes: Standing or seated, press your palms together in front of your chest with your elbows at shoulder height.
Push one hand hard against the other, squeezing your chest.
Hold the tension for the set time breathing normally.
